rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis studies a different alloy (AlCrCoFeNi vs. Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3), a different processing route (arc-melted as-cast vs. selective-laser-melted), and a different intervention (in-situ heating with HTXRD vs. isothermal oxidation of as-printed vs. aged states). It is a completely different kind of study.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses a non-isothermal heating ramp to 1100 °C under vacuum or air, while the target uses isothermal oxidation at 600–1200 °C for up to 96 h. The temperature ranges overlap only partially, and the exposure mode and atmosphere control are fundamentally different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis proposes Al-selective oxidation forming an external Al2O3 scale (Group-III Giggins–Pettit), while the target describes Cr-selective oxidation forming a protective Cr2O3 layer with an inner Al/Ti-rich oxide. These are contradictory mechanisms for the protective scale.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts a thick Al2O3/Cr2O3 duplex scale and Al-depletion-induced phase transformation, whereas the target predicts and observes a Cr2O3-protected scale with higher mass gain for the aged alloy. The predicted property direction and scale architecture are different.
